analysis: Read saved artifacts and source only; no qualification, native/control pair, WSL or GPU was launched.
raw_hash_audit: Delegated timeline evidence owns the complete 27-file raw hash audit; this document does not duplicate it.

target.initial_gap_scope: Includes launch.json, Job creation, bootstrap Popen, attach/identity check and first snapshot; not an isolated observation or native-call measurement.
target.health_stamp_to_post_snapshot_stamp_scop: Clock readings surround job.snapshot plus Python timestamp/dict work; scheduler delays and coarse saved monotonic resolution are included. Zero is not proof of zero cost.

protocol_emission.limit: timestamp_ns is captured before emit serializes/flushes its regular-file stdout. This counts records with pre-error emission labels, not write/fsync completion or physical-media timings.

sentinel.health_stamp_to_post_snapshot_stamp_scop: Clock readings surround job.snapshot plus Python timestamp/dict work; scheduler delays and coarse saved monotonic resolution are included. Zero is not proof of zero cost.

protocol_emission.limit: timestamp_ns is captured before emit serializes/flushes its regular-file stdout. This counts records with pre-error emission labels, not write/fsync completion or physical-media timings.

host_sampling.scope: Host samples include health check and outer Job snapshot followed by requested 50ms sleep; only sample-start timestamps are retained. Host native-call total is not recoverable because per-snapshot identities/history are not saved.

native_count_method.explanation: Three QueryInformationJobObject calls per successful snapshot. Live PID: OpenProcess 1, four wrapped identity calls plus their four diagnostic GetExitCodeProcess probes 8, final _alive probe 1, CloseHandle 1 = 11. Retired PID: OpenProcess 1, three wrapped identity calls plus their three probes 6, CloseHandle 1 = 8. A successful saved snapshot proves these code paths completed under identical pinned source.
native_count_method.excluded: Job creation/attach, unsaved cleanup snapshots, host snapshots, GlobalMemoryStatusEx, shutil.disk_usage, subprocess/CRT/OS-internal calls, and any work outside these saved snapshots. No call durations are inferred.

source_locations.fact: _call constructs native-event dictionaries in memory; no JSON file write or fsync.
Successful snapshot executes 3 Job queries plus OpenProcess, identity authentication and CloseHandle for each enumerated PID. _alive adds unwrapped GetExitCodeProcess probes.
observe appends host-health and windows-history dictionaries in memory; no per-snapshot disk serialization.
Control JSON serializes to bootstrap stdin and flushes the pipe; it is not a snapshot disk write.
launch.json serializes once before bootstrap Popen; transport files are opened before launch.
Final receipt JSON serialization/write occurs after finished_utc and elapsed_s labels, after cleanup, before run returns; no explicit fsync.

Bootstrap JSON protocol records use print(flush=True) to stdout, which runner process.py 467-471 directs to protocol.jsonl. Startup/control records therefore are regular-file-backed serialization and writes, including periodic received PINGs; they are not per-snapshot writes and have no explicit fsync or write-duration brackets.

Fixture grandchild-ready, child-ready and ready records each serialize into a staging file, flush, fsync, hard-link then unlink staging. These writes do occur during startup; no begin/end timing brackets isolate their cost.

Qualification save/trace use JSON plus fsync. attempt and worker-ready are pre-pair; pair-admitted trace precedes thread.start. Host runtime-owned trace precedes GO. No periodic trace is emitted during the failed readiness wait; host samples and snapshots stay in memory.
Duplicated target/sentinel receipts are saved after runner return; windows-controls/control-verdict and host-result are serialized later. They cannot account for earlier startup readiness timeout.

findings.claim: Saved worker runner observations were frequent after the first snapshot; no recurring multi-second observer service gap appears in the saved histories.
findings.limit: This demonstrates those runner loops were serviced. It does not measure fixture child startup, worker readiness-loop scheduling, API cost or an unobserved thread.

findings.claim: Observer work includes repeated native queries, Python dictionary/list construction, retention of history in memory and periodic control pipe JSON; their existence is established by pinned source and saved histories.
findings.limit: Work volume is established; startup slowdown attributable to this work is not measured.

findings.claim: Startup includes once-per-stage launch serialization, bootstrap protocol emission and fixture readiness-file serialization/flush/fsync/publication.
findings.limit: No start/end timing brackets for these operations exist in the saved evidence, so their durations are not isolated.

findings.claim: Bootstrap protocol JSON serialization and regular-file writes occur during startup, including periodic PING-received records; saved pre-error-stamped records contain 27 target PINGs and 26 sentinel PINGs.
findings.limit: stdout is directed to protocol.jsonl and flushed. Physical-media durability, per-record duration and their contribution to startup delay are unmeasured. This is distinct from per-snapshot JSON disk serialization, which is absent.

findings.claim: Observation work, native-call work, fixture startup disk I/O, process launch overhead and Python/OS scheduling may contribute to observed startup latency.
findings.limit: The run has no uninstrumented control, per-operation stopwatch, CPU profile, run-queue trace or thread-scheduling trace; no individual contribution or causal ordering is proved.

findings.claim: Per-snapshot disk JSON serialization caused the failed startup.
findings.reason: Per-snapshot serialization is absent from observe/snapshot. Final large receipt writes are after cleanup and after the readiness deadline failed. In-memory history retention must not be relabeled as concurrent disk writes.

findings.claim: The source proves Python GIL contention or quantifies Python thread scheduling delay as the root cause.
findings.reason: Thread identities and sparse/coarse wall/monotonic labels do not provide run-queue, lock-wait, CPU-time or thread-scheduling measurements.

findings.claim: Subtract requested 25ms/50ms sleeps from observed timestamp gaps to obtain exact observer overhead.
findings.reason: Saved timestamps include sleep rounding, scheduling, other loop work and quantization. They do not bracket active CPU execution.

post_failure_final_serialization_tail.provenance: finished_monotonic_s supplied from saved windows-controls.json runner_states by independent timeline analysis; final receipt elapsed labels are read here.
post_failure_final_serialization_tail.limit: These coarse post-label-to-return spans include final receipt serialization/write and scheduling/return work; they are not an isolated disk or JSON benchmark and occur after the startup deadline error.

limitations: Saved monotonic readings are visibly coarse, often recurring at 15-16ms steps. Zero timestamp deltas cannot establish zero execution cost.
Timestamp gap evidence is a service observation, not a causal performance profile.
Source line references are for the unchanged source hashes in source_pins.
No raw absolute image paths, process IDs, Job handles, nonces or completion contexts are copied into this source-safe report.
